questions.stem: A right-angled triangle has legs of 5 cm and 12 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 = 25 + 144 = 169. c = sqrt(169) = 13 cm. A common mistake is forgetting to take the square root, giving 169.

A right-angled triangle has legs of 7 cm and 24 cm. What is the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: c^2 = 49 + 576 = 625. c = sqrt(625) = 25 cm. Adding the legs (7 + 24 = 31) is a common mistake.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides 8 cm, 15 cm, and 17 cm. Is it right-angled?

options.text: Yes, because 8 + 15 = 23 which is close to 17
No, because the longest side must be less than the sum of the other two

questions.explanation: Check: 8^2 + 15^2 = 64 + 225 = 289. And 17^2 = 289. Since they are equal, the triangle is right-angled (by the converse of Pythagoras' theorem).
